'''Business and economy'''
*[[Nigeria]]n [[Minister of Information and National Orientation (Nigeria)|Information Minister]] [[Lai Mohammed]] announces that the [[government of Nigeria|governmen]]t is indefinitely suspending [[Twitter]]'s operations in the country, saying that the [[social media]] service is being used for "activities that are capable of undermining Nigeria’s corporate existence". The move comes two days after [[President of Nigeria|President]] [[Muhammadu Buhari]] was temporarily suspended from Twitter for posting an inflammatory tweet directed at groups believed to be responsible for [[insurgency in Southeastern Nigeria|attacking government buildings in recent weeks]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/4/nigeria-suspends-indefinitely-twitter-in-the-country (Al Jazeera English)]
*[[United Airlines]] announces it has ordered 15 [[supersonic transport|supersonic jets]] from the [[Denver]]-based aircraft startup [[Boom Technology]], provided the jets meet safety standards, with plans to put them into service in 2029. This is the first time that an airline will use supersonic jets in their service since [[Air France]] and [[British Airways]] retired [[Concorde]] in 2003. [https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-57361193 (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*A [[Mil Mi-8]] helicopter crashes in the [[Alay District]] in [[Kyrgyzstan]], injuring 13 people. [https://akipress.com/news:659066:3_ambulances_dispatched_to_site_of_military_helicopter_crash_landing_in_Alay/ (AKIpress News Agency)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Afghanistan]]
****[[Afghanistan]] reports a record 36 deaths from [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 3,104. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/asia-pacific/afghanistan-records-highest-single-day-death-toll-from-covid-19/2264060 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] surpasses 600,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://www.todayonline.com/world/7748-new-covid-19-infections-malaysia-confirmed-cases-breach-600000-mark (''Today'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan]]
****[[Taiwan]] surpasses 10,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://focustaiwan.tw/society/202106040010 (Focus Taiwan)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Vietnam]]
****The [[Ministry of Health (Vietnam)|Ministry of Health]] approves the emergency use of the [[Sinopharm]] [[BBIBP-CorV]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]], making it the third vaccine to be authorized for use in the country. [https://e.vnexpress.net/news/news/vietnam-approves-sinopharm-covid-vaccine-for-emergency-use-4288933.html (''VnExpress International'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****The [[Government of France|French government]] issues new rules that would allow all vaccinated travellers from the [[European Union]] and seven other "green" countries to enter the [[France|country]] without showing a negative [[COVID-19 test|testing]] result beginning on June 9. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/bonjour-france-welcoming-back-vaccinated-tourists-78080980 (ABC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malta]]
****[[Malta]] reports its first case of the "Delta" [[Lineage B.1.617|B.1.617.2]] variant, which  was originally discovered in [[India]]. [https://www.independent.com.mt/articles/2021-06-04/local-news/Malta-detects-first-Indian-variant-case-health-chief-announces-6736234063 (''The Malta Independent'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency]] approves the usage of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] for people between the ages of 12 and 15, making it the first vaccine to be approved for use in teenagers in the [[United Kingdom|UK]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/health/pfizer-covid-vaccine-children-uk-b1859635.html (''The Independent'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***Some [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] restrictions are lifted in regional [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] as health authorities are confident that the current outbreak is limited to the state capital of [[Melbourne]]. Restrictions will remain in place in [[Greater Melbourne]] for another week. A {{cvt|5|km}} travel limit is extended to {{cvt|10|km}}, and [[QR code|QR]] check ins at public places are now mandatory. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/jun/03/melbourne-lockdown-covid-victoria-restrictions-coronavirus-rules-covid19-explained-5km-radius-masks-compulsory-exercising-home-gatherings-what-you-need-to-know (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Brazil]]
***[[Brazil]]ian health regulator [[Anvisa]] grants a conditional approval for the [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V]] and [[Covaxin]] vaccines. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/brazil-health-regulator-technical-staff-recommend-conditions-any-approval-2021-06-04/ (Reuters)]
*[[Nepal]] reports its first death from [[mucormycosis]], or "black fungus", in a 65-year-old man who was being treated in the [[intensive care unit|ICU]] at a hospital in [[Dhangadhi]] after being diagnosed with [[temporal lobe]] [[encephalitis]]. [https://medicalxpress.com/news/2021-06-nepal-black-fungus-death.html (Medical Xpress)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Belarus]]ian opposition leader [[Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya]] asks the [[United States]], the [[United Kingdom]] and the [[European Union]] to exercise more pressure on the [[government of Belarus|government]] of [[Alexander Lukashenko]]. Tsikhanouskaya, who is currently in self-exile in [[Lithuania]], has been calling for such sanctions since the arrest of activist and journalist [[Roman Protasevich]] on May 23. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/belarus-tsikhanouskaya-calls-eu-uk-us-jointly-pressure-lukashenko-2021-06-04/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2021 Israel–Palestine crisis]]
**[[International protests over the 2021 Israel–Palestine crisis]]
***Pro-[[Palestinians|Palestine]] protesters in the U.S. gather at the [[Port of Oakland]] to attempt to block an Israeli cargo ship from entering the port. Protesters also call for an economic boycott of [[Israel]] following the 11-day conflict. [https://www.sfchronicle.com/local/article/Pro-Palestinian-protesters-at-Port-of-Oakland-16224999.php (''San Francisco Chronicle'')]
**At least 23 runners in [[East Jerusalem]] are injured after Israeli police fired tear gas and stun grenades at people participating in a {{convert|3.5|km|mi||abbr=on}}-run organized to show solidarity with Palestinian families [[Sheikh Jarrah property dispute|facing eviction]] in [[Sheikh Jarrah]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/4/israeli-police-attack-palestinians-running-to-protest-expulsions (Al Jazeera English)]
*[[2020-2021 United States racial unrest]], [[2020–2021 Minneapolis–Saint Paul racial unrest]]
**Protesters face off with officers in [[Minneapolis]] over the shooting death of [[Killing of Winston Boogie Smith|Winston Boogie Smith]]. It was the second night of protests in response to the fatal shooting in the [[Uptown, Minneapolis|Uptown neighborhood]]. The fatal shooting comes as the city has been on edge since the death of [[George Floyd]] and the fatal killing of [[Daunte Wright]] by police officers. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/protest-erupts-minneapolis-over-shooting-death-winston-boogie-smith-jr-n1269729 (NBC News)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Facebook]] announces that it will no longer grant blanket immunity to politicians who use its service, especially if their posts are deemed to be [[Fake news|deceptive]] or [[Internet troll|abusive]]. The announcement comes as Facebook officially bans former [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] from the website until January 2023 after he posted a message which Facebook viewed as supportive of the [[January 6 United States Capitol attack|2021 United States Capitol attack]]. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2021/06/04/facebook-set-scrap-immunity-politicians-posting-fake-news/ (''The Daily Telegraph'')] [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210604-facebook-bans-former-us-president-donald-trump-for-two-years (France 24)]

***The [[Singapore Grand Prix]], originally scheduled for October 3, is cancelled due to [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic|pandemic-related travel restrictions]] imposed on [[Singapore]].
